steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease cookie sheets.

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter, brown sugar and white sugar until smooth. Stir in the eggs, one at a time, and then the vanilla. Sift together the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt, stir into the creamed mixture. Finally, stir in the rolled oats, white chocolate chips and pecans. Drop by tablespoons onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven. Remove from baking sheets to cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: White Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These cookies are absolutely the best!! They really should be named disappearing cookies because they won't stay around long. Set your timer, these cookies are best when they are lightly browned.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was one I have used over and over many times. In place of using the white chips, I have subtituted butterscotch chips instead. Of all the cookies I have made this one is requested the most often. May I also present a hint I have used while cooking these-oven temp. set to 350 degrees and cook cookies for 10 minutes. They are delicious...

FOLLOW EXACTLY as written. Before my first attempt I read ALL reviews and made notes and while trying to incorporate all feedback in, made the first batch. The outcome brought to mind a book I read to my kids, What Kind of Bird Is That?, where the bird picks for himself every best attribute from all his bird friends, but winds up with a hot mess. So, today, I followed the recipe exactly as written, baked 12-14 min and let them cool on the silpat+cookie sheet. My grandkids are gobbling them down as I measure for another batch!! Delicious. I'm using 1 cup of Hersheys Christmas white creme drops that are red and green, and 1 cup of actual white colored chips. So festive. A new but permanent addition to annual holiday baking! Added flour, then chips, then nuts, incorporating each before adding the next, and last, added oatmeal. Not dry at all. Perfect. Yum!

These were great! You won't be sorry you tried these.
 
For those with multiple allergies/intolerances, this is what I used:

- Bob's Red Mill 1 For 1 flour
- Great Value Organic White Baking chips (free of 8 major food allergens)
- Country Crock olive oil plant-blased butter stick and extra virgin olive oil (half and half for the butter)

They were a little hard to hold together, but balled/rolled them in my hands before placing on parchment-lined cookie sheet, and they were fine. 

Turned out fabulous and will make again. Will definitely be added to my 'favorite cookie' list. I ate eight right away, they're that good (and worth feeling a bit sick over, LOL )... I just couldn't stop.

wow. I have found my go-to oatmeal base cookie recipe right here, and I've been baking for over 40 yrs. Let me first say that the 3 cups of flour sort of set my antenna up, as I usually don't see that much flour in a recipe that also has oatmeal but I proceeded as directed. To note, I use the old fashioned rolled oats. The dough was very very stiff, and it took a couple of minutes of grunt to get the flour mixed in, then I had to add the nuts and chips. The dough will appear very 'dry' but not to worry, and don't tinker. don't add milk or anything else. Just proceed. I used a large size pampered chef cookie scoop and did not press down, just placed the scoops on the cookie sheet. 10 minutes was perfect for my oven. The finished result? a cookie that is thick, slightly crispy on the outside, but moist and chewy on the inside, and they looked gourmet-like in appearance. These are absolutely wonderful, and will disappear quick, quick. Texture, flavor, appearance...this cookie has it all. I did not refrigerate the dough, as I saw no need d/t the stiffness of it when mixed together. perfect, perfect. I love the versatility of the recipe. The possibilities are endless with chips, dried fruit, nuts. This made 4 dozen using the large size pampered chef cookie scoop.

This is a very good cookie. The dough itself is a very good base and allows for a lot of variations depending on what you want to do. Some reviewers mentioned that the dough was dry and crumbly but I did not find that that was an issue. I used large eggs as most recipes are calibrated for large eggs. Beat the ‘wet ingredients’ until well blended. Then add the flour mixture and continue to beat for a minute or two until the ‘crumbly’ dough comes together into a smooth easy to use dough. Add the oats, etc and mix well.
Because of allergies I did not add the nuts— but I am sure they would have been good. Instead I used a combination of white chocolate chips and craisins—-1.5 cups of each. Because the craisins are sweeter than the nuts would have been (and because some reviewer’s found the cookie too sweet) I cut the sugar back to 3/4 cup white and 3/4 cup brown. I thought it was perfect this way.
The dough does not spread much in the oven. Unless you want round cookies, flatten each cookie down on the cookie sheet before baking.

I substituted 1C of dried cranberries for the pecans, but that was the only change I made. They were wonderful! Yes, the cookie dough is very stiff and you need to make sure that you incorporate all of the flour and oatmeal that gets left at the bottom of the bowl before you start scooping it out for cookies. This is DEFINITELY a harder dough to mix because of all the extra dry ingredients, but they are also the reason that the cookies are so soft after they're done baking.

Great recipe!Like one review suggested to bake Oatmeal in the oven and then blend it .Instead I used the pan on top stove (for time saving), blended the Oatmeal afterwords. I used whole wheat flour and because my dough was too dry I added 3 Tb. Spoons of unsweetened apple sauce. My family gobbled them up .I will make them again tomorrow but will add lemon zest and lemon juice as per my daughters request .

I was making 1/2 of the recipe and followed it to a T. I tried a few test cookies, but the dough was too dry and crumbly. It was also too sweet. I dumped it and started over. For the next batch, I used a little less white sugar (maybe 1 T less), and softened the butter almost to melting. I added the vanilla with the sugars and butter and creamed them together. Then added the egg. I added the dry ingredients a little at a time and mixed thoroughly after each addition. This made a huge difference! Then, I decreased the oats to 1/2 cup (from 3/4 C), the white chocolate chips to 1/2 C (from 1 C) and then added the 1/2 C pecans. I still had to do a little molding with my hands, but it was so much easier. I baked for 10 minutes, took them out and let them sit for another 2 minutes on the cookie sheet before moving to the cooling rack. The cookies were delicious!
Made 1/2 a batch and they came out perfect. Used a Pampered Chef 2T cookie scoop and baked about 11-12 minutes.

Given the pictures and the worry that there was too much flour, I used only 2 cups of flour instead of 3. I baked them for 11 minutes (after flattening them with a spoon a bit), and they came out flat and chewy, just the way I like them! Next time I'll cut the white sugar by at least half a cup, and I'll add cranberries as well. Cinnamon was a great addition too! Will definitely make this again.

I had self rising flour so I used the called for 3 cups flour plus 1 teaspoon baking powder. I replaced the white chocolate chips with a 4 oz bar of Bakers white chocolate, grated. Baked for 11 minutes. So good and soft yet crunchy. Super good. I will definitely make this recipe again!
I would make this again and again. I replaced the pecans with macadamia nuts and added raisins
Very dry batter. Not a drop cookie. Had to form each cookie using a cookie scoop.
I don't use butter i substitute for applesauce Same amount as you would use with butter So delicious and soft
These are by far the best cookies I have ever made. I will be freezing half the uncooked dough for later to see how they'll turn out from frozen

Made it to the T but used instant oats instead of whole and added dark chocolate chips. So almost to the T lol but it was perfect. 11 minutes for my oven. A yummy cookie that I will be making again and again. It has the perfect chewy texture. Oh and I used plant based butter. Yum. Thank you!
No changes, didn’t use pecans this time. Last time I substituted cranberries for pecans and turned out great. Love this recipe!

Last tray of these delightful cookies in the oven now! Delicious, declared even so by the hubby who isn't often a fan of the oatmeal cookie. I did change up a couple of things per others' suggestions: used 1/3 whole wheat and 2/3 white flours. I did add the cinnamon (because I love it) and some plumped currants. And, I did chill the dough before baking. The dough did seem a little on the dry side, although the finished cookies are not. I rolled my into balls rather than drop from a spoon. The hardest part of these cookies is not eating the dough!
